title: Holistic rollback orchestrator with cost-normalized multi-signal triggers
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Current canary rollback triggers are brittle and tuned per-metric (latency, error rate, throughput, token cost) which leads to noisy false positives and manual parameter tuning for each model/cohort. We need a single orchestrator that ingests multiple SLO signals, normalizes token-cost impact, and produces a single rollback score with tunable sensitivity per deployment. Goals: 1) Combine latency, errors, throughput, and per-token cost into a normalized composite rollback score. 2) Support cohort baselining so that small but important cohort regressions (e.g. high-value customers) can be escalated. 3) Provide automatic threshold tuning using historical windows and holdout baselines to reduce manual rewrites. 4) Integrate with canary traffic controls, A/B experiments, and shadow traffic paths; support graceful evacuation and automatic staged rollbacks. 5) Emit audit events and a clear explanation for every rollback decision for postmortems and compliance.
architecture_notes: Proposal: an orchestration service (rollback-orch) that subscribes to metric streams (Prometheus/Grafana metrics + per-request traces) and to cost telemetry (token accounting). The service will compute: 1) per-metric z-scores relative to cohort baseline, 2) a token-cost-normalization factor that scales cost regressions to latency-equivalent impact, and 3) an aggregated rollback score via weighted, monotonic fusion with exponential smoothing. Tunable knobs per rollout: metric weights, sensitivity, time window, cohort scope, and automatic retraining frequency. Decisions are stored as immutable events in the audit log (Kafka topic + S3 snapshot). The orchestrator exposes a REST webhook used by the rollout controller to adjust traffic or trigger instant evacuation.
acceptance_criteria: A composite rollback score is computed for canary rollouts and available in Grafana (dashboard: 'Rollback Orchestrator / Active Canary Scores')
Auto-rollbacks trigger when composite_score > threshold AND persistence window satisfied (configurable) for >= 5 minutes
Token-cost regressions are expressed in normalized units and visible in the rollback explanation
Canary traffic controller reduces traffic along a staged evacuation policy and records the action in the audit log
Support cohort filtering: at least one cohort (e.g., 'enterprise-large') can be configured to have higher weight and produce alerts independent of global score
End-to-end test suite that simulates latency spikes, increased 5xxs, and token-cost inflation with deterministic outcomes for scoring and action

implementation_plan: Phase 1: Instrumentation - ensure all canary jobs emit latency quantiles, 5xx rate, throughput, and per-request token cost to metrics-pipeline. Phase 2: Service - build rollback-orch with scoring engine and persistence. Phase 3: Integrations - wire to rollout controller for canary/A-B and to shadow routing for alerting only. Phase 4: Auto-tuning - offline job to produce recommended thresholds and adaptive sensitivity. Phase 5: Gradual rollout (internal teams -> beta customers -> GA).
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly aggressive auto-rollbacks could cause unnecessary rollbacks during transient load spikes. Mitigation: require persistence window and traffic-aware hysteresis; default sensitivity conservative for first 4 weeks.
Risk: Cost-normalization misweights token impact for models with bursty token distributions. Mitigation: per-model calibration with holdout windows and manual override flag.
Risk: Complexity of cohort configs leads to misconfiguration. Mitigation: provide sane defaults, templates, and a validation linter in the Console before enabling cohorts.
Risk: Audit/compliance requirements for Private customers. Mitigation: store immutable events in customer-visible logs and encrypt snapshots; add flag to redact PII if needed.
rollout_plan: Week 0: internal rollout for infra and runtime teams only (monitoring, dashboards). Week 2: enable for 2 internal SaaS customers as canary. Week 4: open beta for self-serve customers with opt-in. Week 8: GA with conservative defaults. Each stage requires clear rollback metrics and an ops-runbook for manual override.
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and edge cases (zero-variance cohorts, missing metrics)
Integration test that replays historical canary data and asserts composite score thresholds produce expected actions
Chaos test: introduce synthetic 5xx spike and ensure rollback-orch triggers evacuation under default sensitivity
Shadow mode validation for 14 days: compute scores and compare to manual operator decisions without taking action
E2E: validate webhook actions cause rollout controller to reduce traffic and that audit events are produced
observability_requirements: Expose metrics: composite_score (gauge), per-signal z-scores, decisions_count, rollback_actions_total; traces for scoring decisions with decision_id; Grafana dashboard and alert rule for high-frequency rollbacks. Link to dashboard stub: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rollback-orch
operational_notes: Provide a /dry-run endpoint for controlled testing; enable feature flagging per-customer and per-environment. Add a manual 'freeze rollbacks' toggle in Console for emergency control. Document playbook in runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Rollback+Orchestrator+Runbook
qa_checklist: Can simulate a 10% sustained latency regression and observe score increase
Token-cost increase reported in normalized units and included in explanation
Audit log entry exists for each triggered action with decision rationale
Operators can pause/override auto-rollbacks from Console and see immediate effect
Cohort-based alerts fire independently when configured
notes: Keep scoring explainability high — every composite decision must return a top-3 contributing signals and their normalized impact
Default thresholds should be conservative; we will ship auto-tune as a recommended set of thresholds rather than mandatory updates
Coordinate with Sales/Support for notifications to customers when auto-rollback is enabled (opt-in)
